questions.question: In the ideal near-Earth projectile model, which force acts after launch when air resistance is neglected?
choices: A horizontal force equal to the speed
A force directed along the path

questions.question: What shape is an ideal projectile's path under constant downward gravity?
What is the ideal horizontal acceleration of a projectile with no air resistance?
choices: An acceleration equal to its horizontal speed

questions.question: How is a projectile's velocity analyzed in two dimensions?
At the highest point of an upward launch, which velocity component is zero?
What does a projectile's range measure?
choices: Its horizontal distance from launch to landing

questions.question: Which approximate value is commonly used for gravitational acceleration near Earth's surface?
Why does horizontal speed remain constant in the ideal model?
choices: Gravity balances a continuing horizontal launch force
There is no horizontal net force

questions.question: Why does a projectile's vertical velocity change even at its highest point?
choices: Gravity stops only at the highest point
Its horizontal speed creates upward force
Gravity continues to accelerate it downward

questions.question: Two balls are released from the same height at the same time, one dropped and one launched horizontally. Without air resistance, how do landing times compare?
choices: The horizontally launched ball always lands first
The dropped ball always lands first

choices: Landing speed must be twice launch speed
Landing speed depends only on mass

questions.question: Why can actual projectile motion differ from the ideal model?

Actual launches always have no vertical velocity
